title: NimRTC Profile Schema v1.2
description: Scenario assembly profile (v1.2 — adds the video-scene keys per the remote-desktop plan K4). Strictly ADDITIVE on top of v1.1: every v1.1 profile loads unchanged under this schema; v1.2 profiles add the four optional top-level keys `video_codec_preference`, `video_resolution_floor`, `video_ladder_mode` and `video_content_type`. The C++ loader (src/modules/assembly/src/assembly.cpp) reads them into the matching `assembly::Profile` fields; a key that is absent leaves the engine default in place (codec preference "h264", resolution floor "720p", ladder mode "quality", content type "camera"). The ladder mode vocabulary and the per-profile defaults are tabulated in docs/plan/video-pipeline-v2-plan.md §B.7.3 (OD-3(a)); the content-type vocabulary follows ADR-022 (screen content as a content type).

video_codec_preference.description: v1.2 additive — preferred video codec for this scene. A preference, not a requirement: the negotiated codec is the one both peers support. For a screen-content scene it drives the encoder's screen-coding tools (remote-desktop plan B8; ADR-021 for the bundling posture). Omitted = engine default "h264".

video_resolution_floor.description: v1.2 additive — the adaptation ladder's resolution floor: the lowest resolution the ladder may step down to. Configurable per scene / machine class, because a scene that reads text cannot fall below the floor without destroying the product (remote-desktop plan D2). Omitted = engine default "720p".

video_ladder_mode.description: v1.2 additive — the ladder's adaptation mode: "quality" (quality-first — spend the budget on resolution / fidelity) or "smoothness" (smoothness-first — spend it on frame rate). The per-profile defaults are tabulated in docs/plan/video-pipeline-v2-plan.md §B.7.3 (OD-3(a)); the engine default is quality-first. Omitted = engine default "quality".

video_content_type.description: v1.2 additive — the content type of the video source. "screen" selects the screen-coding tools, the content hint and the ROI handling; a screen capture is NOT "a camera with a huge resolution" (ADR-022; remote-desktop plan RD-3). Omitted = engine default "camera".

video_stream_weights.description: v1.2 additive — the declared per-stream bandwidth shares (remote-desktop plan D5). The session's bandwidth estimate is divided between the video streams by weight; the rule itself lives in exactly one place (src/engine/src/bandwidth_allocation.hpp) and is shared with the audio path. The key is the stream's stable id ("default", "screen", "camera", ...) — the same id NimRTCEngine::add_video_stream() takes — and the value is the stream's relative weight. A weight of 0 means "this stream takes nothing from the pool"; the default weight is 1 (an even split). The map is declarative, not constructive: a declaration for a stream the session never creates is inert, not an error. The runtime override (NimRTCEngine::set_video_stream_weight()) always wins over the declaration. Omitted = every stream splits the pool evenly.

transport.description: v1.1 additive block — declares the transport strategy and the (media_stack, control_stack) pair. See docs/plan/transport-strategies.md §2 for the five named strategies.

strategy.description: Use-case strategy id. Empty string (or omitted) = engine compile-time default ('browser-call').

stack.description: Media-stack factory id. 'webrtc-classic' = libjuice + wolfSSL + usrsctp (default); 'raw-udp-arq' = bare UDP + ARQ (no SCTP, no browser interop); 'webrtc-quic' = v1.x WebTransport (not in v0.12.0).

max_p99_ms.description: Optional p99 latency budget. The Selector records the value but does not enforce it (v0.13+ may add a validator; see transport-strategies.md §6 #4).

control.description: Control-plane stack declaration. When `enabled` is false, control traffic rides the media stack's DataChannel (SCTP).

enabled.description: Enable a side-stack for the control plane. When false, control rides the media stack's DC (SCTP).

stack.description: Control-stack factory id. Only meaningful when `enabled` is true.

reliability.description: Reliability model for the control plane.
